description:
## What

The write side. Agent gains a host-write API; Coder takes ownership of *what's in Agent's buffer*.

New on Agent:

- `Agent.push_message/2` — append a single `AgentMessage` to `loop.messages`.
- `Agent.set_messages/2` — wholesale rewrite (used by ticket 3 for compaction, ticket 4 for navigation; introduced here so the API is complete).

Widen Agent's message type:

```elixir
@type agent_message ::
        AI.Message.t()
        | OctoPi.Coder.Session.CompactionSummaryMessage.t()
        | OctoPi.Coder.Session.BranchSummaryMessage.t()
        # | other synthetic types as they land
```

`convert_to_llm` (from opi-y0a.1) is the boundary that flattens synthetic types — Agent stores them natively, the wire never sees them.

Coder.Loop write points:

- `init` — seed Agent: `Agent.set_messages(agent_pid, SessionStore.path(:leaf, to: :latest_compaction))`
- `add_user_message` / `add_entry` for non-streamed types — after tree append, call `Agent.push_message`.

**Ownership rule** (origin-based, not type-based):

- Agent writes streamed assistant + tool_results from its own turns (already does this; unchanged).
- Coder writes everything else (user prompts, synthetic types, future bash side-channel events).
- Neither side double-writes the same message.

## Why

After this ticket, Agent's `loop.messages` is the canonical working buffer for the LLM, kept correct by the host. The bypass (`messages_provider`) is no longer load-bearing — `loop.messages` already represents the right chain.

## Files

- `apps/octo_pi_agent/lib/octo_pi/agent.ex` — public `push_message/2`, `set_messages/2`.
- `apps/octo_pi_agent/lib/octo_pi/agent/loop.ex` — handle_call clauses; widen `loop.messages` element type.
- `apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/loop.ex` — `init` seeds Agent; `add_user_message` / `add_entry` mirror to Agent.

## Out of scope

- Compaction / navigation `set_messages` callsites (those land with the trigger inversion in opi-y0a.3 / opi-y0a.4).
- Dropping `:path` (opi-y0a.5).
- Inlining `MessageLog` (opi-y0a.6).

## Done when

- Agent has `push_message/2` and `set_messages/2`.
- Agent's `loop.messages` accepts synthetic types without crashing in `convert_to_llm`.
- Coder seeds Agent at init from `SessionStore.path(:to: :latest_compaction)`.
- A new test verifies: after `Coder.add_user_message`, the Agent's `loop.messages` has the user message at the tail.
- `messages_provider` can be removed from Coder.Loop.init's installation step (still defined on Agent for now if opi-y0a.1 hasn't deleted it; this ticket doesn't depend on that).
title: Coder mirrors writes into Agent's transcript via push/set APIs
